messages:
alex_k: Heads-up — eu-west1 had a burst of ECC/XID signals at ~03:14; detector spammed and the cordon workflow fired across multiple AZs, causing Slurm backlog.
maya: Oof. did the nodes actually show persistent errors or were these transient spikes from telemetry noise?
alex_k: Mostly short-lived spikes. A few nodes bumped ECC counts for ~20-40s and then cleared. The cordon sequencer has no debounce and acted immediately.
jin: Paste the health tail snippet if you have it.
alex_k: ```
2026-02-28T03:14:12Z gpu-health — dev-gpu-az1-092 ECC=6 XID=1 last_seen=12s
2026-02-28T03:14:19Z gpu-health — dev-gpu-az2-011 ECC=7 XID=0 last_seen=7s
2026-02-28T03:14:21Z cordon-controller — dev-gpu-az1-092 cordon requested by signal
```
maya: That matches the integration test failure pattern we saw last week — telemetry bursts lead to many concurrent cordons.
stella_ops: We need a gating/sequencer so a telemetry burst doesn't cascade into multi-AZ capacity loss.
sam: Proposed responsibilities for sequencer:
  - dedupe identical signals for same card within a short window
  - per-AZ concurrency semaphore (eg 1 active drain per AZ)
  - global token-bucket rate limit for drains
  - SLO-aware bailouts (if free GPU pool falls below threshold, queue or downgrade to soft-quarantine)
jin: Add a transient-window debouncer (60–90s): only escalate to full cordon if errors persist. If cleared, cancel queued action.
alex_k: Example gate config we sketched: ```json
{ \"per_az_parallel\": 1, \"global_rate_per_min\": 4, \"slo_min_free_gpu_fraction\": 0.05, \"transient_window_sec\": 90 }
```
maya: Also allowlist fatal signals to bypass the gate (PCIe fatal, persistent ECC > 100, kernel oops).
stella_ops: Add a cheap local probe before cordon: run nvml sample + 20s micro-memtest; if probe clears, cancel the cordon. That reduces false-positive evacuations.
drain-bot: [automated] received 8 signals in eu-west1, queued 4 drains, starting 1 per az :gear:
jin: For Slurm, drains need a preempt/reschedule window. Sequencer should call the Slurm-handshake with a delay param (default 120s) and include job-reschedule hints for interactive jobs.
sam: Fallback policy: if sequencer sees >N queued drains in a region, notify ops channel and downgrade some to soft-quarantine (taint but no eviction).
alex_k: Canary plan: roll sequencer behind a feature flag to us-central1, monitor drain rate, job reschedule rate, interactive tail latency, and failed-job counts.
maya: I'll add observability: per-signal histograms, gating decision counts, cancelled drans, and SLO alerts (free GPU fraction, job eviction rate).
stella_ops: Next steps: alex_k to write design doc + open PR; jin to spec Slurm handshake contract; sam to prototype token-bucket + per-AZ semaphore.
alex_k: Draft design doc posted: https://go/repo/notes/seq-drain. Will PR today.
jin: I'll start on Slurm handoff spec and a kubectl-to-slurm shim.
sam: Prototyping token-bucket + semaphore this week — will post bench results.
\alm: (note) we should also consider region-aware stagger windows so we never run concurrent drains in >2 AZs for a single failure domain.
maya: Good call. also surface a rollback toggle that cancels queued drains when rollback enabled.
stella_ops: Thanks team — priority is preventing another eu-west1 capacity blip.
drain-bot: [automated] queued drains: 3 active, 1 pending; will escalate to ops if pending >5 for 5m.
alex_k: assigning PR to @jin and @alex_k.
maya: :+1: thanks.
